title: PostgreSQL Full-Text Search: tsvector, tsquery, and GIN Indexing
realWorldScenario: Customers complain that searching for "wireless headphone" in your e-commerce store fails to return products titled "Wireless Bluetooth Headphones" when using `LIKE '%wireless headphone%'`. Furthermore, the `LIKE` query takes 900ms.
questionStatement: Explain PostgreSQL native Full-Text Search. Compare `tsvector` and `tsquery`. Explain text normalization (tokenization, stop words, stemming with Snowball dictionary). Provide the SQL to create a generated `tsvector` column, a GIN index, and a ranked search query using `ts_rank()`.
expectedConcepts: tsvector lexemes and positional weights (A, B, C, D)
tsquery boolean logic and phrase distance (<->)
Snowball stemmer reducing words to root forms
Stored generated column + GIN index pattern
hints: Why does LIKE '%wireless headphone%' fail to match plural "headphones"?
What dictionary stems words in PostgreSQL?
Use websearch_to_tsquery for natural user search inputs.
